description.en-US: Open any article in the language you're learning and this extension tells you one thing: what share of it you already know. Reading works when you understand almost everything — around 98% of the words — because that's when you can infer a new word from context instead of stopping to look it up. Below about 95% you're decoding, not reading, and that's the difference between a book you finish and one you abandon on page four. The problem is you can't tell which side of that line a page falls on by looking at it. So count it. HOW IT WORKS Click the icon on any page. The extension reads the article text, measures it against the vocabulary band you've set, and shows you: • The percentage of the page you already know • Whether it's comfortable, a stretch, or too hard as it is • The words that are new to you • Which frequency band the page is actually written for, so you can see how far off it is If it's too hard, "Read it at my level" opens Beeblio, which fetches the same article and can rewrite it at your level while keeping the meaning. WHY FREQUENCY BANDS Words follow a steep curve: a small set does most of the work. The 1,500 most common Spanish words cover roughly 80% of ordinary text; the next ten thousand buy you far less. Learning them in frequency order means the next word you learn is the most useful one left. The bands here — 300, 800, 1,500, 3,000, 5,000, 8,000, 12,000 — are that curve, and they're what the measurement is against. LANGUAGES Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Dutch, Polish and Turkish. SET YOUR LEVEL ONCE Pick the language you're learning and your band. If you don't know your band, there's a free two-minute test at beebl.io — 24 words, one at a time, know it or not yet. PRIVACY The extension sends the text of a page to Beeblio's servers to measure it, and only when you click the icon. It does not run on pages you haven't asked it to, it has no access to your browsing history, it asks for no account, and it sets no tracking cookies. Your language and band are stored in your browser profile. Full policy: https://beebl.io/privacy Beeblio is a reader for language learners — free to use, with an optional paid plan. Made by Digideal LLC.

summary.en-US: Measure any page against the words you already know, then read it at your level. Ten languages, no account needed.

description.en-US:
Hubort gives you one search box for every AI conversation you have: across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, across separate accounts of the same service, and across browser profiles. It all stays on your own computer. If you use AI in more than one place (a work account and a personal one, a couple of different assistants, several browser profiles, a shared family plan), your conversations are scattered across sessions that can't see each other. Each service's own search only looks inside the account you're signed in to. Hubort gives you the view across all of them. HOW IT WORKS
  1. Install the Hubort desktop app for Windows: https://hubort.app/download It keeps your archive in a database on your own disk.
  2. Install this extension in each browser profile you use AI in.
  3. Pair it: choose "Pair a Browser" from the Hubort tray icon and type the seven-digit code into the extension. Your archive stays yours, even on a PC shared by several Windows accounts.
  4. Tick the services this profile should read, and give each account a name, such as "Work" or "Personal". Your browser asks for access to a service's site only when you tick it.
From then on the extension keeps your archive up to date in the background, and the Hubort app searches all of it at once. SUPPORTED SERVICES • ChatGPT • Claude • Gemini, with several Google accounts in one browser • Grok Every service is included. There is no per-service charge. WHAT YOU GET, FREE • Full-text search across every chat, with whole-word and title-only matching, filtered by service, account, folder or note • Instant results: the archive is a local database, not a web request • Folders and sticky notes that cross account and service lines • Pinning, archiving and your own ordering • Export to Markdown, any time • Optional backup to your own Google Drive • Usage-limit indicators for Claude and Grok, so you can see which account still has room • Light and dark themes, four colour schemes HUBORT PRO ADDS • Ask Your Archive: questions answered from your own chats, written by the AI provider you choose, on your own API key • Usage Insights: what you use each service for, how much, and when you hit its limits • Related Chats: similar chats in your other accounts, worked out on your own computer • Live Sync: your chats kept current in a folder of Markdown files (an Obsidian vault, say) or in your own Notion workspace PRICING Hubort is free for up to 2 sources. A source is one account on one service, however many browsers sync it. Every install starts with 14 days of Hubort Pro, with no card and no email. Hubort Personal syncs every account, and Hubort Pro adds the four features above. Both come monthly, yearly, or as a one-time purchase with 12 months of updates. Payment happens on hubort.app, never in this extension. If you stop paying, Hubort goes back to the free version and deletes nothing. Full pricing: https://hubort.app/pricing PRIVACY Your conversations are never sent to us. Hubort has no server to send them to: they are read with the sessions this browser is already signed in to and written to a database on your own disk. No ads, no tracking, no account to create. This extension talks only to the AI services you switch on and to the Hubort app on your own computer (127.0.0.1). It only reads: it never sends, renames, archives or deletes anything in your accounts. A few things can leave your computer, each only because you chose it in the app: Ask Your Archive's excerpts (to your own AI provider), Live Sync to your own Notion, a Drive backup, a problem report when you press Send, and usage reports if you switch them on. The privacy policy lists every one: https://hubort.app/privacy REQUIREMENTS • Windows 10 or 11, with the Hubort desktop app installed first. Without it, the extension has nowhere to put your conversations. • An account on at least one supported service, signed in to in this browser profile. GOOD TO KNOW Hubort reads each service's web interface automatically, on a schedule. Some services' terms restrict automated access, so using Hubort may be inconsistent with them. You can lengthen the sync interval, or turn scheduled syncing off and sync only when you choose. Hubort is an independent product, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or xAI. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok are trademarks of their owners.

description.de: WhoGetsMyData shows which companies a website connects to while you browse. Click the toolbar button to see, for the page you are on: • every company your browser contacts, with the services it uses (for example Google Analytics, the Meta Pixel or Hotjar) • which of them track you • where each company is based • a link to the free, detailed privacy report of the website on whogetsmydata.com The number on the toolbar button tells you at a glance how many companies a page connects to. COUNTED IN YOUR BROWSER The add-on looks at which servers a page contacts and compares them with a database of more than 1,500 known services and 1,200 companies that comes with the add-on. Counting happens in your browser. You need no account, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose to help (see below). FULL PRIVACY REPORTS WhoGetsMyData is a free privacy project. Every website report shows a privacy score, a cookie banner test in a real browser (what loads before a choice, after "Reject" and after "Accept"), all trackers and third parties with evidence, where the companies are based, and whether the privacy policy names the providers the website loads. OPTIONAL: HELP THE PUBLIC DATABASE If you want, the add-on tells our scanner which websites you visit, so that it can check websites that are not in the database yet and notice when a website adds trackers. This is off until you turn it on in the welcome page or in the add-on menu, and Firefox asks you separately for the permission to share browsing activity. When it is on, the add-on shares for each website: its domain (for example example.com), the known services it contacted, other third-party domains it contacted, the version of the add-on and the kind of browser. It never shares anything that identifies you (no ID, no account, no cookies), addresses of pages, search terms, page content, form input or when you visited a website. The add-on does not run in private windows. Each website is shared at most once a day, not right away, and together with a few others picked at random, so that no browsing history comes together on our server. The server keeps only counters per website. You can exclude single websites and turn helping off at any time. PERMISSIONS • Access your data for all websites: to see which servers the current tab contacts. The add-on only reads which servers a page contacts and never changes pages. Request addresses are compared with the patterns of known services in your browser and are not kept. • Access browser tabs: to know which tab a request belongs to and which website is open. • Storage and alarms: to keep the counts per tab in memory and your settings, and to send waiting websites every few minutes, only when helping is on. No analytics, no ads and no code from other companies. The package contains readable source code only. More about the add-on: https://whogetsmydata.com/extension Privacy policy: https://whogetsmydata.com/privacy#extension

description.en-US: Tayseer Downloader is a download manager for Windows, and this add-on connects it to Firefox. It adds a small "Download" button over videos while they play: click it, see the available qualities with their file sizes, pick one, and the download starts immediately in the Tayseer Downloader desktop app. On a playlist you can download every video in one click. It also hands the files you download in Firefox to the app, which downloads them faster over several connections and lets you pause and resume them. IMPORTANT: this add-on is a companion to the Tayseer Downloader desktop app for Windows. The app must be installed and running on the same computer; the add-on does not download anything by itself. Get the app (30-day free trial, then a subscription) from Tayseer Store: https://tayseer.store/download FEATURES - A "Download" button appears at the top corner of a playing video. It stays subtle and becomes fully visible when you move the mouse over the video. - A quality menu: every video quality the site offers (for example 1080p or 4K) with its file size, plus audio only (MP3 or M4A). - One click on a quality starts the download in the app, which shows the progress and saves the file. - "Whole playlist": on a playlist (for example on YouTube) the menu shows a "Whole playlist (N videos)" section that downloads the entire playlist in one click, numbered in order, into a folder named after the playlist. - Faster browser downloads: when you download a file in Firefox (an archive, an installer, an ISO image, a document, or any file larger than 2 MB), the add-on offers it to the app. If the app takes it, it disappears from Firefox's download list and the app downloads it over multiple connections, with pause and resume. Web pages are never taken, and if the app is closed or its option to take over browser downloads is off, Firefox downloads the file normally, so nothing is lost. - "Open in the app" for links that need more options. - Works on most video websites, including YouTube, in full-screen players and in embedded players. - Interface in 19 languages, including English, Arabic, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian, Turkish, Russian, Japanese and Korean (follows the browser language). - Private by design: no account, no ads, no analytics. The add-on talks only to the app on your own computer (127.0.0.1); it sends nothing to any server. ABOUT THE TAYSEER DOWNLOADER APP (Windows 10/11, 64-bit) - Downloads videos and audio from YouTube (videos, Shorts, whole playlists and courses, saved numbered in order), TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, X and more than 1000 other sites, in every available quality up to 8K, or as MP3. - Downloads any direct file link (ZIP, EXE, ISO, PDF and more) over multiple connections for more speed, with pause and resume, even after you close the app. - Catches downloads started in the browser and takes them over. - Starts with Windows and waits quietly in the system tray. - Interface in 20 languages. - 30-day free trial, then a subscription. HOW TO USE 1. Install and open the Tayseer Downloader desktop app. 2. Install this add-on, then reload the tabs that were already open. 3. Play a video and click "Download" at its top corner. 4. Pick a quality (or the whole playlist): the app starts downloading at once. 5. Download any file in Firefox as usual: if the app is running (taking over browser downloads is on by default in its Settings), it takes the download over automatically. If the app is closed, the add-on opens it for you (Firefox asks once for permission) and then shows the qualities. Please download only content that you own or have permission to download.

summary.en-US: Download button over videos and whole playlists; browser downloads go to Tayseer Downloader for faster, resumable downloads.

description.en-US:
PaneMux lets you use the web without reaching for the mouse. Press f and every link gets a couple of letters: type them and PaneMux clicks it. j and k scroll, / searches the page, H and L go back and forward, J and K switch tabs. Everything runs locally: no network calls, no accounts, no data collection. It starts gentle. A two-minute interactive tutorial opens on install, the Classic preset turns on only the essentials, and ? shows every key that's switched on, in plain English, with a search box. Click into any text box and PaneMux steps aside until you press Esc. The toolbar button pauses it on the current site in one click, for web apps that have their own shortcuts. When you want more, switch to Power User (or pick features one by one):
  • Command bar (:) with fuzzy completion: close every tab matching a pattern, pin or reload a group of tabs, split the screen. Closing several tabs always shows them first, and every close has an Undo button.
  • Text objects: yap copies the paragraph you're reading as Markdown, dah hides a heading and everything under it, cit lets you edit a line of text right on the page.
  • Page outline (gO): the page's headings as a foldable outline. Walk it with j and k and the page follows; pin it while you read.
  • Visual mode for elements: walk the page with h/j/k/l, hide things, copy them as Markdown, open them in a clean reading pane.
  • Macros: record q a … q, replay with @a, across page loads and tab switches.
  • Tab registers: save a set of tabs into a letter and reopen them later.
  • Undo tree: closed tabs, hidden elements and form edits, with u, Ctrl-r and a clickable history panel.
  • Splits: two windows tiled side by side, with keys to jump between them.
  • Vimgolf: score your keystrokes against the mouse clicks they save, with a leaderboard.
Every key can be changed or switched off in Settings. The status strip at the bottom of the window always shows which mode you're in and never blocks a click. PaneMux is open source (MIT): https://github.com/PaneMux/panemux

Visual mode selects page elements, not characters.
gO: an outline of the page's headings. The page follows as you move.
yap copies the paragraph you're reading, while a Vimgolf round keeps score.
? lists every key that's switched on, searchable.
A two-minute tutorial that waits for the real keys.
Presets, searchable keys and per-key reset.

description.en-US: Automatically open the local version of a website when your development server is running. Enter your website URL and localhost port once. When you visit a matching URL, Redirect to Local checks your local server. If it responds, the extension redirects you to localhost while preserving the full path and query string. If your server is unavailable, you stay on the original website. With website https://example.com and port 3000: https://example.com/test?a=b → http://localhost:3000/test?a=b Deep links, nested paths, and query parameters carry over automatically. Automatic availability checks: Checks localhost before each matching page navigation. Fallback to the original website: If localhost is unreachable or doesn’t respond within 1.5 seconds, navigation continues normally. Preserves paths and query strings: Open the corresponding local page without manually editing the address. Saved settings: Your website URL and localhost port are stored locally in Firefox. Pause and resume: Temporarily stop redirects without losing your configuration. Your pause preference persists across browser restarts. Exact host matching: Only the configured hostname and port match. Subdomains are treated separately. Open Redirect to Local from Firefox’s extensions menu. Enter your development server’s port, such as 3000. Enter the website URL, such as https://example.com. Click Save settings. Start your local server and visit the website. Use Pause redirects whenever you want to browse the remote website while your local server is running. The extension sends a lightweight HEAD request to http://localhost:PORT/. Any HTTP response confirms that the server is reachable—even if the root path returns an error such as 404. Matching works across HTTP and HTTPS source URLs. The local destination always uses HTTP. If you enter a website URL containing a path, the extension saves its origin and matches all paths on that host. Redirects apply to ordinary top-level GET navigations. Form POST submissions, embedded frames, and background requests are not redirected. Existing tabs are not automatically moved between the remote and local website. Redirect to Local has no analytics or external service. Your website URL, localhost port, and pause preference are stored locally in Firefox. Website access is required to detect matching navigations and check localhost availability. Firefox 142 or later A local development server accessible at http://localhost:PORT View the source code or report an issue on GitHub (https://github.com/itsberkelium/redirect-to-local). Created by itsberkelium (https://berke.dev).

summary.en-US: Redirect a configured website to localhost when your development server is running.

description.en-US:
GoodConvertPDF is a browser extension built around local processing. It helps users organize web content, text materials, structured data, images and chat records from your browser into PDF documents that are easier to save and share. More than a simple "export to PDF" button, it delivers a complete workflow covering quick conversion, preview adjustment, content organization and post-processing for PDFs. Many conversion and editing operations run directly inside your browser on your local device. Document content will not be uploaded to conversion servers for these local tools. This extension supports multiple content sources. You can start from the current webpage, convert it to PDF and adjust page parameters in a dedicated workspace. It also handles plain text, CSV, JSON, logs, pasted message threads or chat transcripts, formatting them into structured printable documents. For images, it combines multiple JPG, PNG or WebP files into one PDF. For conversations, it formats pasted email threads or exported chat logs into clean, archive-ready transcripts. It also includes Pro-level chat import capability, which can import conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other supported sites when the matching webpage is open. The full workspace is one of the core features of GoodConvertPDF. It works for webpage-to-PDF conversion as well as HTML content and image collections, offering real-time preview and fine-grained layout control. You can pick common paper sizes including A4, A3, A5, Letter and Legal, or define custom dimensions. You may also toggle portrait/landscape orientation, measurement units, scaling, output quality, preset margins and custom margin values. Beyond basic layout settings, the workspace lets you prepare webpages before export: auto-scroll for lazy-loaded pages, export only a selected region of the page, hide unwanted elements, and restore the original page state afterward. This means it is not limited to saving webpages; it lets you organize documents inside your browser first, then export PDFs optimized for reading and archiving. For webpage export, the extension uses browser debugging and scripting capabilities to process the active HTTP or HTTPS page. Certain special unsupported pages will be rejected. The preprocessing module temporarily modifies page rendering before printing and restores the page after export. The element selector lets you click to pick specific sections for export, hide distracting content before conversion. This works especially well for saving articles, reports, instructions and documentation pages, producing cleaner, better-structured PDFs. The document processing area expands the use cases further. The extension accepts CSV, JSON, plain text, log files and conversational text, rendering them into printable documents. It includes CSV parsing logic with delimiter detection, quoted values and multi-line content support. JSON is parsed and normalized into tables for object arrays, 2D arrays, single objects or scalar values. Plain text gets cleaned and standardized, and the conversation parser handles message threads and email-style text. The interface offers encoding options such as UTF-8, GB18030, Windows-1252 and Shift JIS, reflecting compatibility with text imported from many sources. Beyond PDF generation, GoodConvertPDF includes local PDF post-processing tools. You can add multiple PDFs, reorder them, select page ranges and merge them into one output file. It also supports adding text watermarks and cover pages before download, with preview available. These operations run locally on your device, and temporary files disappear once the tab closes. The code also checks for unreadable or unmodifiable PDFs to improve stability. The extension supports local HTML documents and resource packages. It can read ZIP archives containing local resources, enforces limits on file count and size, blocks unsafe paths and sanitizes content. This shows attention to security and stability when rendering HTML sources. Meanwhile, it includes account and subscription logic: login redirects, locally stored auth tokens, account status checks and display of logged-in, offline, free or Pro states. Some chat export and online entry points are tied to login and upgrade flows in the popup. However, local-first mode exists in the configuration, which hides cloud-related web entry points when cloud features are disabled. Overall, GoodConvertPDF is best understood as a versatile PDF creation and organization toolkit. It lets you turn webpages into PDF with one click, refine layout and clean page content before export, assemble PDFs from text, data, images and conversations, and further merge PDFs, add covers or watermarks afterward. It is a complete workflow for users who prefer document processing to happen locally within the browser and download results directly to their machine.
  • Convert the active webpage to PDF and preview / adjust export settings in a dedicated workspace.
  • Create PDFs from plain text, CSV, JSON, logs, email threads and chat transcripts.
  • Merge multiple JPG, PNG and WebP images into a single PDF file.
  • Page cleanup tools: export selected regions, hide unwanted elements and restore the page afterward.
  • Layout controls: paper size, orientation, scaling, output quality and margin settings.
  • Post-process existing PDFs: merge, reorder, select page ranges, add cover pages and text watermarks.
  • Import AI chat content on supported webpages for Pro export workflows.
  1. Open the extension popup and choose your content type: webpage, text, images, structured data or conversations.
  2. For webpages, open the full workspace, select the active tab and view the preview.
  3. Adjust paper size, orientation, margins, scaling and output quality as needed.
  4. Use page cleanup tools before export: select target regions or hide distracting elements.
  5. For text, data or conversations, paste or load content in the document panel to generate a printable view.
  6. Download the generated PDF once conversion finishes. For further editing, go to the PDF tool page to merge files or add covers and watermarks.
  7. If you use account or Pro features, log in as prompted to check your current plan status.
When login is enabled, this extension stores authentication tokens locally and checks your account status. The local PDF conversion and editing tools run inside your browser on your device. Document content will not be sent to conversion servers.

description.en-US:
Yabancı dildeki videoları okumadan, kendi dilinizde dinleyin. DubThis.video, YouTube ve Udemy videolarındaki altyazıyı yakalar, seçtiğiniz dile çevirir ve çeviriyi videonun zamanına oturan bir seslendirmeye dönüştürür. Video oynatıcının üzerinde açılan küçük bir panelden her şeyi yönetirsiniz. Şu an tüm özellikleriyle herkese ücretsiz. Hesap açmanız ya da kart bilgisi girmeniz gerekmez. NELER YAPAR
  • Öngörülü çeviri: Altyazıyı birkaç saniye önden toplar ve çevirir. Konuşma sırası geldiğinde çeviri hazırdır, ses geriden gelmez.
  • Zaman-senkron dublaj: Çeviriyi tarayıcınızın konuşma sentezi ile seslendirir. Cümle süreye sığmazsa konuşma hızı otomatik artırılır, gerekirse video geçici olarak yavaşlatılır.
  • 12 dilde canlı çeviri: Türkçe, İngilizce, Almanca, İspanyolca, Fransızca, İtalyanca, Portekizce, Rusça, Arapça, Japonca, Korece ve Çince.
  • Ekranda çeviri: Çeviriyi altyazı olarak da gösterir. İsterseniz orijinal altyazıyı gizleyebilirsiniz.
  • Altyazı görünümü: Konum, genişlik, punto, renk, saydamlık ve hizalamayı ayarlayın.
  • Oynatma hızı: 0.25x ile 4.00x arası. Seçtiğiniz hız yeni videolarda korunur.
  • Video kaydedici: Videoyu doğrudan yakalar veya ekran kırpma kullanır. Dosya webm ya da mp4 olarak bilgisayarınıza iner.
  • Senkron göstergesi: Altyazı kaynağını, sıradaki cümle sayısını ve sesin videodan ne kadar saptığını panelde anlık görürsünüz.
NASIL KULLANILIR
  1. YouTube veya Udemy'de altyazısı olan bir video açın.
  2. Panel sağ üstte belirir. Gizlemek ya da açmak için Alt + C veya araç çubuğundaki simgeyi kullanın.
  3. Ses sekmesinden dublajı açın ve hedef dili seçin. Ayarlarınız sonraki videolarda hatırlanır.
Not: Dublaj için videoda altyazı (otomatik oluşturulanlar dahil) bulunmalıdır. Ses kalitesi, işletim sisteminizin sunduğu seslere bağlıdır. GİZLİLİK Ayarlar yalnızca tarayıcınızda saklanır. Çeviri için yalnızca altyazı metni Google Çeviri'ye gönderilir. Videonun sesi veya görüntüsü hiçbir yere gönderilmez. Kayıtlar yalnızca cihazınızda oluşturulur. Eklentide analitik, reklam veya izleme kodu yoktur. YouTube, Google LLC'nin; Udemy, Udemy, Inc.'in tescilli markasıdır. DubThis.video bağımsız bir araçtır ve bu şirketlerle bağlantılı değildir.

description.en-US:
SERP Exporter turns the Google search results page you already have open into clean, structured SEO data in seconds. Extract organic results and Local Pack listings, including ranking position, title, URL, domain and result type, then copy or export the data in the format that suits your workflow. Use SERP Exporter to:
  • Copy URLs or unique domains
  • Copy complete search results
  • Paste directly into Excel or Google Sheets with TSV
  • Export structured SERP data to CSV
  • Copy results as clean Markdown
  • Format SERPs specifically for analysis in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other AI tools
SERP Exporter automatically removes common tracking parameters from URLs, giving you cleaner data for competitor research, SERP comparisons, link research and analysis. Where available, it also identifies the Google search market, such as Australia, and includes it with your exported SERP data. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your search results are not uploaded or stored anywhere.

developer_comments.en-US:
SERP Exporter reads the Google search results page you already have open, pulls out organic results and Local Pack ("map pack") listings (position, title, URL, domain, type), and lets you copy or export them in several formats:
  • Copy URLs (one per line)
  • Copy domains (unique, one per line)
  • Copy full results (position + title + URL + type)
  • Copy as TSV (paste straight into Excel/Sheets)
  • Copy as Markdown (readable numbered list — for docs/notes)
  • Copy for AI analysis (a Markdown table — fewer tokens, easier for an LLM to compare rows)
  • Export CSV (structured file with SERP metadata)
Every exported URL has common tracking parameters (utm_*, gclid, fbclid, srsltid,msclkid, and similar) stripped automatically, so exports and deduplication aren't polluted by ad-click/analytics noise. Parameters that actually change page content are left untouched. Where reliably detectable (via the SERP's gl= parameter or a country-specific Google domain like google.com.au), the search market is captured alongside the Google host — e.g. "Australia" — and included in the popup, CSV and AI exports. It's omitted rather than guessed when it can't be determined (e.g. a plain google.com search with no gl param).

description.en-GB:
Turn hardsubbed web videos into interactive language lessons. YuzuLingo uses fast, on-device text recognition (OCR) to make burned-in hardsubs hoverable, searchable, and easy to read directly inside your browser's video players. 🌟 KEY FEATURES • Hover-to-Lookup: Hover over burned-in hardsubs on YouTube, Bilibili, and open web video players to get instant dictionary definitions. • Furigana & Pinyin Overlays: Toggle phonetic reading guides directly above Kanji (Japanese) and Hanzi (Chinese) characters in real time. • Active Recall Blur Zones: Mask hardsubs with customizable blur or solid covers to test your listening first, then hover or hold a hotkey to reveal. • 5 Language Engines: Comprehensive OCR and dictionary lookup support for Japanese, Chinese (Simplified & Traditional), Korean, English, and Spanish. • 100% On-Device & Private: Video frames and OCR text recognition run entirely inside your browser. Video content is never uploaded to external servers. 🎯 PERFECT FOR • Japanese learners watching anime or YouTube channels with burned-in hardsubs. • Chinese learners watching Bilibili, Youku, or dramas with hardcoded Chinese subtitles. • Korean, English, and Spanish learners looking to read native video content effortlessly. • Immersion language learners practicing Mass Immersion or active listening methodologies. 🚀 GET STARTED IN 10 SECONDS
  1. Add YuzuLingo to your browser and pin it to your extension toolbar.
  2. Open any video player containing burned-in subtitles.
  3. Draw a zone over the subtitle area and hover over words to view lookups.
